issue.title: Fix bench compare crashing on agentic suites

affected_files.role: cmd_compare (125-164) calls runner.run at :147 with no kind() branch; compare subparser (343-355) also lacks --max-turns
run_tests() :62 does task['tests'] -> the KeyError site. No change required.
loop.run()/summarize() is the agentic execution path cmd_compare must call; summarize() already emits kind='agentic' and agent_score
kind(name) is the dispatch predicate cmd_run already uses; read-only for this fix
build() already branches on summary kind=='agentic'; renders agentic metrics with zero change once compare writes the right summary
match_reasons: downstream consumer; confirms no change needed

affected_files.role: swap_to/restart in cmd_compare's loop; any new test must stub these so no real endpoint restarts
NEW - regression test covering the agentic path through compare (AC3)

analysis.summary: cmd_compare (benchkit/cli.py:125-164) never learned about agentic suites. cmd_run (cli.py:78) and cmd_harness both branch on kind(args.suite), but cmd_compare calls runner.run(get(args.suite), cfg, on_result=_print_result) unconditionally at cli.py:147. Agentic task dicts carry id/difficulty/prompt/files/check/oracle and no 'tests' key, so runner.run -> work() -> run_tests() hits task['tests'] at benchkit/runner.py:62 and raises KeyError: 'tests'. This is a gap, not a regression: it has existed since commit ce5723b introduced the agentic suite and added the kind() branch to cmd_run only. Nothing downstream needs changing - benchkit/agentic/loop.summarize() already stamps kind='agentic' with agent_score/mean_efficiency/mean_tool_calls/mean_turns, and report.build() already branches on that key.
analysis.details: Failure chain: ./bench compare A B --suite agentic -> cli.main() -> cmd_compare -> serving.swap_to(model) -> runner.Config(...) -> runner.run(get('agentic'), cfg) -> ThreadPoolExecutor(work) -> run_tests(task, code, timeout) -> prog = code + task['tests'] -> KeyError. Secondary gap: the compare subparser has no --max-turns, which the agentic loop needs (cmd_run's parser defines it at cli.py:330), so a parser change is required alongside the dispatch branch. The structural defect is duplicated dispatch logic: three commands each decide independently how to run a suite, and one of them was never updated. AC3 ('the two commands cannot diverge again') points at a shared dispatch helper rather than a copy-pasted if/else.

options.name: Copy the kind() branch into cmd_compare
options.summary: Mirror cli.py:78 inside cmd_compare and add --max-turns to the compare subparser.

files_to_modify.changes: In cmd_compare, branch on kind(args.suite): call loop.run(tasks,cfg,on_result=_print_agentic,max_turns=args.max_turns) for agentic, runner.run otherwise. Add --max-turns to the compare subparser.

pros: Zero risk to the one-shot path
cons: Third copy of the same dispatch if/else - the exact divergence AC3 forbids
options.rejection_reason: Triplicates the dispatch logic and ships no test, so it fails acceptance criterion 3 outright.

options.name: Shared suite-dispatch helper plus a regression test
options.summary: Extract one _execute_suite(suite, tasks, cfg, ...) helper used by both cmd_run and cmd_compare, add --max-turns to compare, and add a test that pins the agentic path through compare.

files_to_modify.changes: Add module-level _execute_suite(suite_name, tasks, cfg, max_turns, keep_code=False) returning (summary, results) and dispatching on kind(); call it from cmd_run (replacing lines ~78-84) and from cmd_compare (replacing line 147). Add --max-turns to the compare subparser.

files_to_create.purpose: unittest.TestCase asserting _execute_suite routes agentic suites to loop.run and codegen suites to runner.run, and that cmd_compare uses it - with serving.swap_to/current_model and the run functions stubbed so no endpoint restarts and no results/ writes occur.

options.test_strategy: unittest, repo style (sys.path insert, TestCase); monkeypatch benchkit.serving.swap_to/current_model, benchkit.runner.run and benchkit.agentic.loop.run; assert the agentic suite reaches loop.run and the resulting summary carries kind='agentic'; assert core16 still reaches runner.run unchanged.
pros: One dispatch site, so run and compare structurally cannot diverge again (AC3)
Regression test with no live endpoint and no results/ writes
Adds the first test coverage for cli.py
cons: Touches cmd_run as well as cmd_compare, slightly widening the blast radius
Mild merge-conflict risk with #37, which edits cmd_compare's finally block
options.risk_details: Pure refactor of an if/else into a helper; both branches already exist and are exercised by ./bench validate and ./bench run

options.name: Rebuild cmd_compare as a campaign runner
options.summary: Restructure cmd_compare into a generic setup-loop that dispatches over suite kind, harness and serving config in one pass.
cons: Effort L against an effort:S high-priority bug
Also blocked by #19's restart guardrail, which is unrelated to this crash
Holds a shipping bugfix hostage to a design-heavy feature
